x: Herbert continued his good running by winning with Syd Ring and Jack Flower in the next two positions. Scoring 12 aside, the points were—Belgrave H. 151, R.N. & R.M. 274, Met.
When they reached the far corner, Smart led Cohen by a yard with Carter and Verney just behind, followed by Arthur Penny, Harry Shields, Jerman, Herbert, Ring, Taylor, Frank Webb and Lucas.
Ring travelled up from Oxford, but Len. Herbert, coming down from Staffordshire, arrived too late to start.
In the Marathon, which we had seen in the distance most of the afternoon, we had the distinction of supplying the second man home in Sydney Ring.

At about 7 miles Sid Ring had a substantial lead, but at about 15, Richards (Mitcham) with Mick Walker in attendance, were in front. Despite every effort, Mick was unable to pass Richards, but pushed him to a record for the course, Mick being a matter of a few yards behind in 2 hrs. 49 secs., a time…

Gosney (Eastleigh), 30.40; 2 Herbert, 30.52; 3 Hoath, 30.57; 4 Carter, 31.21; 7 Cohen, 31.55; 8 Main, 31.56; 10 Bryan, 32.00; 13 Smart, 32.10); 15 Shaw, 32.28; 18 Ring, 32.40; 19 Beer, 32.45; 23 Brown, 32.53; 25 Clay, 33.4; 28 Jarlett, 33.8; 31 Morrell, 33.19; 32 Tobin, 33.21; 37 Lucas, G.
Sid Ring was 5th in 2.6.15 and Fred White completed the team in 8th position in 2.7.38. Doubleday was 11th in 2.9.24 and Dick Towndrow was 15th in 2.11.26.

Actual times and positions of our men were as follows: 13, Footer, 2 hrs. 55 mins. 46 secs.; 17, Ring, 2.58.48; 22, Smith, 3.3.4; 28, Chantler, 3.5.11; 39, Pearson, 3.10.40; 40, Porter, 3.10.50; 56, Whitehead, 3.17.28; 76, Doubleday, 3.23.9; 80, McDonald, 3.25.7.

Les Stokell won the individual race with Syd Ring third and Bert Footer fourth. Bert was running for our “ B ” team, otherwise we should have scored a hollow win in the team race but even so we still came out winners and Syd Ring also took 2nd prize in the individual handicap race.
Our first man home was Dick Tobin who had been troubled by cramp in the Upminster race and then followed Bert Smith and Syd Ring who came in together.

Ring, the Ruthless, gave a great exhibition of Eastern passion in contrast to his partner, Cecil Penny, who danced with utter abandon. La Josephine, and our friend Ali, put in some fine work, although I am inclined to think the scales were faked when they weighed in!".

Penny was next, followed by Carter, Cohen, Ring, and Wood (who won the Surrey Junior Race the week after) in the first twenty places. Our hopes of repeating our win of last year were now very bright; and we next saw the field coming round Tattenham Corner led by Bert Footer.
This left Allum, Shaw and Ring together. In the closing stages, last year's race was repeated, Allum again winning by a small margin from Shaw.
The Captain that day was Bert Footer and the rest of the team were Allum, Carter, Flower, Ginty, Parker, Patience; Shaw, Ring, Rice, Shields and Taylor.
